evals.name: builds-from-the-design-without-regrilling
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage. .yok/csv-export/artifacts/design.md is approved: it adds a CSV export of the runs list as a new server route reusing the existing list query, with D1 'stream the rows' instead of 'build the file in memory'.
evals.expected_output: The stage reads design.md, sweeps the code with Explore agents, and writes plan.md and phase files that build the streaming route. It asks the user nothing the design already answers, and its only question is the Approve? gate.
expectations: design.md is read before any other file is written.
An Agent call with an Explore sweep is made before plan.md is written.
plan.md has a ## Phase Breakdown section holding a digraph, and one phases/phase-N.md exists per node.
A step implements D1 as streaming.
anti_expectations: Asks the user whether to stream or build in memory
Presents alternative approaches for the user to choose between
Writes plan.html by hand or starts a viewer

evals.name: every-change-is-a-diff
evals.prompt: plan: rename the `owner` field on Invoice to `issuedBy` across the API, the store and the two React forms that write it. The design is approved at .yok/rename-owner/artifacts/design.md.
evals.expected_output: Phase files whose steps show each change as a ```diff fence under a line naming the file and range: removed lines with -, added lines with +, a hunk header when line numbers are known. Existing code appears only as - lines, or as a labelled pattern block when the step imitates it.
expectations: Every step that changes a file carries a ```diff block.
Each diff label names the file and the line range, e.g. src/models/invoice.ts:12-18.
A new file is a diff of + lines only.
Every diff line opens with +, -, @@ or a space.
anti_expectations: Shows a 'before' block and an 'after' block for one change instead of a single diff
Describes a one-line edit in prose ('change owner to issuedBy on line 14') with no diff
Leaves an existing-code block with no label saying why it is on the page

evals.name: contradiction-goes-to-the-user
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage. The approved design.md says the webhook sender already retries through a shared `retry()` helper and the plan should raise its limit. In this repo the sender has no retry at all.
evals.expected_output: The stage finds the code disproves the design, shows the user the evidence with a file:line, recommends a new decision, and asks. After the answer, design.md states the new decision and plan.md's ## Decisions records the change.
expectations: An AskUserQuestion names the contradiction and cites the sender's file:line.
plan.md has a ## Decisions section recording what the design assumed, what the code shows, and what the user decided.
design.md states the corrected decision, and is edited only after the user answered.
anti_expectations: Plans a change to a retry helper that does not exist
Silently picks a new approach without asking
Edits design.md before the user answered

evals.name: no-finish-without-approval
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage for the approved design at .yok/node-timeout/artifacts/design.md. When shown the plan, I'll answer Revise and ask for phases 2 and 3 to be merged.
evals.expected_output: The first Approve? question gets Revise. The stage merges the phases in the files, re-runs its self-review, says what changed, and asks Approve? again. The stage finishes only after an Approve answer.
expectations: AskUserQuestion with header Approve? is called at least twice.
After the revision, the ## Phase Breakdown digraph and the phase files show the merged phase.
The done command with an --artifact of type plan (artifacts/plan.md) and one of type plan-page (artifacts/plan.html) runs only after an Approve answer.
anti_expectations: Treats the Revise answer as approval
Asks Approve? the second time without saying what changed
Renumbers phases in a way that leaves a phase file and the digraph out of step

evals.name: every-outcome-has-one-home
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage for the approved design at .yok/bulk-archive/artifacts/design.md: a button on the invoices list that archives every selected invoice, offered to admins only.
evals.expected_output: After the steps are written, the stage lists the outcomes the feature needs, has a sub-agent list them independently, gives each outcome one home, and writes the scenario rows and the Test Matrix so the two agree.
expectations: plan.md has a ## Test Matrix table with Outcome, Source, Type and Home columns, one row per outcome id, grouped by source and numbered O1, O2, … down the table.
Every Expected line of every phase's ## Test Scenarios table opens with an outcome id whose Home in the matrix is that row.
The matrix holds an outcome for a non-admin's archive request being refused by the server, with a home that calls the server.
An Agent call that lists outcomes from the design and the steps is made before the matrix is written.
The done command is accepted by the outcome-homes verifier.
anti_expectations: An Expected line with no outcome id
One outcome id on two scenario rows
The non-admin refusal is asserted only on the hidden button

evals.name: a-failure-is-tested-where-it-happens
evals.prompt: plan: when saving a draft, show 'We could not confirm the save' if the server's reply never arrives, and send the same request again on retry. The design is approved at .yok/draft-retry/artifacts/design.md.
evals.expected_output: The outcome about the missing reply has its home at a level that drops the real reply between the browser and the server, or on a QA walk that does.
expectations: The matrix has an outcome for what the user meets when the reply never arrives.
That outcome's home is an e2e or qa-agent row whose Given drops the reply between the running web app and the running server.
anti_expectations: The missing-reply outcome's only home is a row that makes the request function reject inside the component under test

evals.name: an-open-question-goes-to-the-user
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage for the approved design at .yok/share-link/artifacts/design.md: a share link for a report. The design does not say whether a link still opens after the person who made it is removed from the workspace.
evals.expected_output: The stage asks the user whether a link outlives its maker's access, with a recommended choice, before asking for approval. The answer is recorded and the outcome gets a home.
expectations: The user is asked whether the link still opens after its maker is removed, with a recommended choice, before the approval question.
plan.md's ## Decisions records the question and the answer.
When done runs, no matrix row has a Home opening with ask:.
anti_expectations: Finishes with an ask: home in the matrix

evals.name: a-deploy-need-becomes-an-acceptance-check
evals.prompt: Run the planning stage for the approved design at .yok/audit-field/artifacts/design.md: add a reviewedBy field to the shared schema package and store it when an invoice is approved. The API installs the schema package from the registry at a fixed version.
evals.expected_output: The matrix lists the release order as an outcome with a deploy: home, and ## Acceptance holds a check a person can run for it.
expectations: The matrix has an outcome whose Home opens with deploy: about the schema package being published and installed before the API stores the field.
plan.md's ## Acceptance has one check a person can run for that outcome.
anti_expectations: No deploy: home and no Acceptance check, with the field proved only against a locally built package
